purpose: Dronabinol is used to help relieve nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy when other anti-nausea medicines have not worked well enough. It is also used to help improve appetite and prevent weight loss in people with AIDS who have lost a lot of weight.
how_it_works: Dronabinol is a man-made form of THC, the active ingredient found naturally in cannabis (marijuana). It works by connecting to certain receptors in your brain that help control nausea, vomiting, and appetite. By activating these receptors, it helps calm your stomach and can make you feel more like eating.
common_side_effects: Feeling 'high' or euphoric, dizziness, drowsiness, confusion, feeling unusually happy or silly, increased heart rate, dry mouth, and increased appetite (sometimes called 'the munchies'). Some people may also feel anxious or have difficulty thinking clearly.
warnings: This medication can affect your thinking, coordination, and judgment, so do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. It can be habit-forming, so use it exactly as prescribed. Tell your doctor if you have a history of mental health problems, heart disease, or substance abuse. Avoid alcohol and other sedatives while taking this medicine. It is a controlled substance (Schedule III). Do not use during pregnancy unless your doctor specifically advises it.
typical_dosing: For nausea from chemotherapy, the usual dose is 5 mg taken 1 to 3 hours before chemotherapy, then every 2 to 4 hours after, up to 4 to 6 doses per day. For appetite in AIDS patients, it is usually started at 2.5 mg taken twice a day, before lunch and dinner. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on how you respond and any side effects you experience.
